transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm seeking help because I've been feeling extremely depressed, sad, and empty for the past two months. This is a massive shift from the previous nine months, where my mood was constantly elevated and irritable, and I had overflowing energy.
During those nine months of elevated mood and high energy, did you require hospitalization or were you unable to function in your daily life because of how intense those symptoms were?
No, I was never hospitalized during that time. I'm not really sure or haven't thought much about whether it affected my ability to function, though.

Did you experience any significant problems at work, school, or in your relationships during that period, such as being fired, getting into frequent arguments, or engaging in risky behaviors that were out of character for you?

Yes, I actually had a lot of trouble during those nine months. I was so irritable that I got into constant, heated arguments with people over the smallest things, and I started doing really risky, impulsive things like reckless driving that were completely out of character for me.

During those nine months of high energy and irritability, did you ever experience any hallucinations, such as hearing voices or seeing things that others couldn't, or did you hold any unusual beliefs that were clearly not true?
No, I didn't experience anything like that. I never heard voices, saw things that weren't there, or held any unusual beliefs during those nine months.

Even without hospitalization or hallucinations, did these impulsive behaviors and arguments cause a marked impairment in your social or occupational functioning, or were you still able to maintain your normal daily responsibilities?

Yes, it caused severe strain, especially because my reckless spending and constant arguments created a lot of financial distress and damaged my relationships. However, I was still somehow able to keep going to work and handle my basic daily responsibilities. It was just an incredibly chaotic and stressful time for both me and my family.

Was there any period during those nine months where you felt like you didn't need to sleep at all or only needed a few hours of sleep, yet still felt completely rested and full of energy the next day?

Yes, absolutely, that happened all the time during those nine months. I would sleep for only two or three hours a night—sometimes not at all—but I'd wake up feeling completely refreshed and full of energy. I never felt tired and was always ready to start my day immediately.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [Bipolar I Disorder, Bipolar II Disorder]. The patient described a period of elevated/irritable mood lasting nine months with decreased need for sleep, reckless spending, and impulsive behavior. Crucially, the patient reported that these symptoms caused 'marked impairment' in social and occupational functioning (financial distress and damaged relationships). According to DSM-5-TR criteria, a manic episode is distinguished from a hypomanic episode by the presence of marked impairment in social or occupational functioning. Since the patient experienced marked impairment, this meets the criteria for a manic episode, favoring Bipolar I Disorder over Bipolar II Disorder.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a 9-month period of elevated/irritable mood, decreased need for sleep, and impulsive behavior (reckless driving, spending) causing significant interpersonal and financial distress, followed by a major depressive episode. While the patient was not hospitalized, the severity of functional impairment and the presence of marked behavioral disturbance align with Bipolar I Disorder.
